To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) joint linkage–linking disequilibrium mapping can improve the mapping efficiency for drought tolerance in maize, and (ii) haplotype-based analysis can further improve the mapping efficiency.

joint linkage–linkagedisequilibrium mapping is an effective approach to detect QTL underlying drought tolerance in corn, and the candidate genes for the QTL identified in our study are involved in the control for flowering and detoxification pathways that are associated with cellular damage due to stress.

joint linkage–linking disequilibrium mapping with haplotes identified 18 QTL for ASI that were not detected by parallel linkage–LD analysis, and that the use of haplotyes increased the mapping efficiency, with a significant QTL having PVE up to 34%.

joint linkage–LD mapping using diverse inbred lines can improve mapping efficiency and identify more QTL than linkage mapping alone, and that haplotypes are a powerful approach for increasing the efficiency of QTL detection.
